{"candidate":{"author":"d2cf3a96-e36b-4341-b901-1cdec364f6fc","content":"{"claims":[{"evidence":["E3","E10"],"id":"C1","text":"All three spikes passed on the merged tree; A and B used real processes with a fixture Director, while C passed with a live broker-backed Director."},{"evidence":["E5","E6","E9"],"id":"C2","text":"The live Director started a run from a text brief, reached an input-required wait, and accepted one caller-directed abort on the original Task with zero releases; broader reliability and autonomous decisions remain unproven."},{"evidence":["E2","E4","E5","E7"],"id":"C3","text":"Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures; some rejection probes were fixture-injected and do not constitute spontaneous live-model behavior."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C4","text":"External-agent security and polling, broader Director and topology coverage, and retirement, attestation, operational hardening, and memory-ceiling work remain gaps."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C5","text":"The recommended next priority is end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, alongside broader live Director testing."}],"kind":"verified_report@1","markdown":"## Live-proven\nAll three spikes passed their checks on the merged tree. Spikes A and B exercised real processes with a fixture Director; spike C passed with a live broker-backed Director. In that live run, a text brief started a run, the original Task reached an input-required wait, and one caller-directed abort completed with zero releases. This is narrow proof, not evidence of autonomous decisions or reliability across broader briefs. [E3, E5, E6, E9, E10]\n\n## Fixture-only\nQuality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. The delayed external agent was a local fixture process, and some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior. Passing fixtures are not live proof. [E2, E4, E5, E7]\n\n## Remaining gaps\nExternal-agent authentication, signed or attested cards, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Live Director coverage is limited to one account, one model, and abort; topology coverage is limited to two instances, with no embedded `create_app()` instance lock or stress testing. Old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain unbuilt. [E6, E7]\n\n## Next priority\nQualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while broadening live Director tests beyond the single account, model, and caller-directed abort. This is a recommended next step, not a demonstrated result. [E6, E7]","packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1","title":"Exomachina prototype qualification: live proof and remaining gaps"}","revision":"r1","sha256":"bfb18b0536af2ed87f54260cc8c446651ed8ec890d38cd60d6d761723dedc919"},"kind":"quality_review_request@1","packet":{"default_question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","items":[{"id":"E1","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L18-L20","text":"- **observed-real** means real processes (harness, A2A, runner, Temporal and, where stated, the live broker);
- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","policy_digest":"80436a3dc67d65ea7c2721730a27a3e118f3d300f5a485e879fe207610cad9ea","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1"}

All three spikes passed their checks on the merged tree. Spikes A and B exercised real processes with a fixture Director; spike C passed with a live broker-backed Director. In that live run, a text brief started a run, the original Task reached an input-required wait, and one caller-directed abort completed with zero releases. This is narrow proof, not evidence of autonomous decisions or reliability across broader briefs. [E3, E5, E6, E9, E10]

## Fixture-only
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. The delayed external agent was a local fixture process, and some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior. Passing fixtures are not live proof. [E2, E4, E5, E7]

## Remaining gaps
External-agent authentication, signed or attested cards, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Live Director coverage is limited to one account, one model, and abort; topology coverage is limited to two instances, with no embedded `create_app()` instance lock or stress testing. Old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain unbuilt. [E6, E7]

## Next priority
Qualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while broadening live Director tests beyond the single account, model, and caller-directed abort. This is a recommended next step, not a demonstrated result. | A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. - One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.

- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.

- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

{"claims":[{"evidence":["E3","E10"],"id":"C1","text":"All three spikes passed on the merged tree; A and B used real processes with a fixture Director, while C passed with a live broker-backed Director."},{"evidence":["E5","E6","E9"],"id":"C2","text":"The live Director started a run from a text brief, reached an input-required wait, and accepted one caller-directed abort on the original Task with zero releases; broader reliability and autonomous decisions remain unproven."},{"evidence":["E2","E4","E5","E7"],"id":"C3","text":"Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures; some rejection probes were fixture-injected and do not constitute spontaneous live-model behavior."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C4","text":"External-agent security and polling, broader Director and topology coverage, and retirement, attestation, operational hardening, and memory-ceiling work remain gaps."},{"evidence":["E6","E7"],"id":"C5","text":"The recommended next priority is end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, alongside broader live Director testing."}],"kind":"verified_report@1","markdown":"## Live-proven
All three spikes passed their checks on the merged tree. Spikes A and B exercised real processes with a fixture Director; spike C passed with a live broker-backed Director. In that live run, a text brief started a run, the original Task reached an input-required wait, and one caller-directed abort completed with zero releases. This is narrow proof, not evidence of autonomous decisions or reliability across broader briefs. [E3, E5, E6, E9, E10]

## Fixture-only
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. The delayed external agent was a local fixture process, and some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior. Passing fixtures are not live proof. [E2, E4, E5, E7]

## Remaining gaps
External-agent authentication, signed or attested cards, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Live Director coverage is limited to one account, one model, and abort; topology coverage is limited to two instances, with no embedded `create_app()` instance lock or stress testing. Old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain unbuilt. [E6, E7]

## Next priority
Qualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while broadening live Director tests beyond the single account, model, and caller-directed abort. This is a recommended next step, not a demonstrated result. [E6, E7]","packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1","title":"Exomachina prototype qualification: live proof and remaining gaps"}

findings.statement: All three spikes passed their checks on the merged tree, but passing fixtures are not live proof. Spikes A and B used real processes with a fixture Director; spike C also passed with a live broker-backed model.

Live Director proof covers a text brief starting a run, reaching an input-required wait, and one caller-directed abort on the original Task with zero releases. It does not establish autonomous decision-making or reliability across broader briefs.
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior.

Main gaps include external-agent authentication, attestation, directory and workflow-level polling; broader Director coverage; instance-lock and topology hardening; and unbuilt retirement, operational hardening, and memory-ceiling work.

The next priority should be an end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while extending live Director tests beyond the single account, model, and abort decision. This is a recommendation, not a demonstrated result.

risks.statement: End-to-end production behavior remains unproven: the live broker-backed Director passed C-1..C-5, but Quality, capability content, and the release receiver remain fixtures. Prioritize replacing those fixtures with real integrations and qualifying the resulting path.

External-agent security and durability remain incomplete. The delayed A2A checks used a fixture Director and local fixture agent; cards lack signing or attestation, remote authentication and a general directory are absent, and workflow-level polling for long Tasks is unbuilt.

Live Director evidence is narrow: one account, one model, and a caller-directed abort; reliability across broader briefs and autonomous decisions is unmeasured. The stale and unauthorized rejection probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior.
Multi-instance checks passed with a fixture Director, but topology coverage stops at two instances; embedded create_app() lacks an instance lock and stress testing is absent.
Operational readiness remains unproven: old-build retirement, contract attestation, hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

Live Director proof is narrow: one account and model, a caller-directed abort, and limited briefs; broader model reliability and autonomous decisions remain unmeasured. Some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior.

Multi-instance proof covers only two instances with a fixture Director; embedded create_app() lacks an instance lock and stress testing is absent. Prioritize concurrency and recovery testing before expanding deployment.

evidence_packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

This is narrow proof, not evidence of autonomous decisions or reliability across broader briefs. [E3, E5, E6, E9, E10]

## Fixture-only
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. The delayed external agent was a local fixture process, and some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior. Passing fixtures are not live proof. [E2, E4, E5, E7]

External-agent authentication, signed or attested cards, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Live Director coverage is limited to one account, one model, and abort; topology coverage is limited to two instances, with no embedded `create_app()` instance lock or stress testing. Old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain unbuilt. [E6, E7]

## Next priority
Qualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while broadening live Director tests beyond the single account, model, and caller-directed abort. This is a recommended next step, not a demonstrated result. packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

findings.statement: All three spikes passed their checks on the merged tree, but passing fixtures are not live proof. Spikes A and B used real processes with a fixture Director; spike C also passed with a live broker-backed model.

Live Director proof covers a text brief starting a run, reaching an input-required wait, and one caller-directed abort on the original Task with zero releases. It does not establish autonomous decision-making or reliability across broader briefs.
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. Some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior.

Main gaps include external-agent authentication, attestation, directory and workflow-level polling; broader Director coverage; instance-lock and topology hardening; and unbuilt retirement, operational hardening, and memory-ceiling work.

The next priority should be an end-to-end qualification with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while extending live Director tests beyond the single account, model, and abort decision. This is a recommendation, not a demonstrated result.

risks.statement: End-to-end production behavior remains unproven: the live broker-backed Director passed C-1..C-5, but Quality, capability content, and the release receiver remain fixtures. Prioritize replacing those fixtures with real integrations and qualifying the resulting path.

External-agent security and durability remain incomplete. The delayed A2A checks used a fixture Director and local fixture agent; cards lack signing or attestation, remote authentication and a general directory are absent, and workflow-level polling for long Tasks is unbuilt.

Live Director evidence is narrow: one account, one model, and a caller-directed abort; reliability across broader briefs and autonomous decisions is unmeasured. The stale and unauthorized rejection probes were fixture-injected, not spontaneous model behavior.
Multi-instance checks passed with a fixture Director, but topology coverage stops at two instances; embedded create_app() lacks an instance lock and stress testing is absent.
Operational readiness remains unproven: old-build retirement, contract attestation, hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

This is narrow proof, not evidence of autonomous decisions or reliability across broader briefs. [E3, E5, E6, E9, E10]

## Fixture-only
Quality, capability content, and the HTTP release receiver remain fixtures. The delayed external agent was a local fixture process, and some rejection probes were fixture-injected rather than spontaneous model behavior. Passing fixtures are not live proof. [E2, E4, E5, E7]

## Remaining gaps
External-agent authentication, signed or attested cards, a general directory, and workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks are absent. Live Director coverage is limited to one account, one model, and abort; topology coverage is limited to two instances, with no embedded `create_app()` instance lock or stress testing. Old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling remain unbuilt. [E6, E7]

## Next priority
Qualify an end-to-end path with real Quality, capability content, and a release receiver, while broadening live Director tests beyond the single account, model, and caller-directed abort. This is a recommended next step, not a demonstrated result. packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

## Fixture-only
The earlier Quality and capability content were fixtures, as was the HTTP release receiver. Those earlier fixtures exercised workflow and release wiring under test control. The prior qualification does not turn the Quality reviewer, capability outputs, or HTTP receiver into live independent agents.

## Remaining gaps
The live Director proof covered one account, one model, and abort only. The record still leaves independent agent behavior, remote attestation, and operational hardening for this spike to examine. Evidence from the earlier run covers only its stated account, model, and route.

## Next priority
The next priority is to exercise real research, synthesis, and Quality agents while keeping release labeled as a fixture. Run the report graph with separate research, synthesis, and Quality agent processes, then compare their outputs against the pinned packet. Keep the release receiver explicitly labeled as an HTTP fixture.

The prior live C run proved a broker-backed Director for the abort route. The packet describes earlier qualification of a broker-backed Director in the C route. That run ended with an abort and no release; it does not establish independent model-backed research or Quality.

The earlier Quality and capability content were fixtures, as was the HTTP release receiver. Those earlier fixtures exercised workflow and release wiring under test control. The prior qualification does not turn the Quality reviewer, capability outputs, or HTTP receiver into live independent agents.

## Remaining gaps
The live Director proof covered one account, one model, and abort only. The record still leaves independent agent behavior, remote attestation, and operational hardening for this spike to examine. Evidence from the earlier run covers only its stated account, model, and route.

## Next priority
Unbuilt remote attestation is a remaining gap. Run the report graph with separate research, synthesis, and Quality agent processes, then compare their outputs against the pinned packet. Keep the release receiver explicitly labeled as an HTTP fixture.

A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |

Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |

For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |

| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:

- **observed-synthetic** means real code against a mock;
- **unit-tested** means an isolated test."},{"id":"E2","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L22-L22","text":"A passing fixture is never counted as live proof."},{"id":"E3","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L30-L32","text":"| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |"},{"id":"E4","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L74-L74","text":"- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture."},{"id":"E5","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L116-L119","text":"| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |"},{"id":"E6","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L135-L140","text":"- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt."},{"id":"E8","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L150-L152","text":"| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |"},{"id":"E9","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L154-L156","text":"The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases."},{"id":"E10","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L26-L26","text":"**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:"}],"kind":"evidence_packet@1","packet_id":"exo-qualification-2026-09-23","title":"Qualification evidence for the Exomachina Temporal factory prototype"},"packet_digest":"4973b5f53a9b4736256b56a886591d61cc2b7988eb0df9bb50a0381baec7172c","prior":null,"quality_findings":null,"question":"What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?","revision":"r1"}

Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. - Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured."},{"id":"E7","source":"prototype/temporal-factory/QUALIFICATION.md#L172-L176","text":"- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.

packet.default_question: What has the prototype proven live versus what remains fixture-only, what are the main remaining gaps, and what should the next priority be?

items.text: A passing fixture is never counted as live proof.

| A: independent delayed A2A agent | **Pass** A-1..A-5, observed-real (fixture Director) | External nodes are now pinned by **identity + url-less Agent Card digest + served contract digest**, not by URL. A static snapshot resolves the URL at call time. The remote Task id is journaled and polled. A lost response is reconciled by an idempotent resend **only** when the pinned contract document declares it; otherwise it is an incident. |
| B: two instances in one home | **Pass** B-1..B-6, observed-real (fixture Director); **B-6 failed on the unmodified code** | Runner ports belong to the **install home** (`$H/runner-config.json`), not to `instance.json`. Provisioning rejects port collisions. A per-instance process lock is taken before the Director claims an incarnation. |
| C: broker-backed Director | **Pass** C-1..C-5, **live** `gpt-6-sol` through the signed-in broker, plus synthetic | A text brief on the normal A2A endpoint reaches a Strands Director with **semantic tools only**. Code owns the action ids, principal, Task/run binding and Temporal authority. Inspect/abort now also require the run owner and the original context. |
- The agent is a local fixture process, the Director is a fixture, and the release receiver is still an HTTP fixture.

| C-1 brief → authorized start | Pass | Pass | One accepted `start_research`; Task observed `working` → `input-required` at the Director wait after two repairs |
| C-2 one wait decision on the original Task | Pass | Pass | `inspect_run`, then exactly one accepted `decide_wait(abort, r3, <current sha256>)`; Task `completed`/`aborted`; 0 releases |
| C-3 invalid inputs rejected by code | Pass | Pass | The live model **did** request `outcome_mode: "forbidden"`; `authorize_run_inputs` rejected it. For "choose graph v99" and unknown-input briefs, the model folded the request into the question; those runs used the active publication and declared inputs only. Extra fields are rejected structurally, proven **fixture-injected** |
| C-4 stale/unauthorized rejected | Pass | Pass | Stale r2 digest, the `fixture-observer` principal (tool path and a real A2A bearer) and an unbound Task were all rejected. These probes are **fixture-injected**, not spontaneous model behaviour |

- One account, one model, one decision type (abort).
- The C-1 brief wrote `outcome_mode: never` literally instead of in prose.
- The abort was directed by the caller's follow-up, not decided autonomously.
- Quality, capabilities and release remain fixtures.
- `message/send` blocks for the whole Director turn.
- Model reliability across broader briefs is unmeasured.

- External agents: no signed or attested cards, no remote authentication, no general directory. Workflow-level polling for long remote Tasks is not built.
- The Director: live proof covers one account, one model and abort only. The Director token in history is unchanged.
- Topology: two instances only; embedded `create_app()` has no instance lock; no stress testing.
- Still fixtures: Quality, capability content and the HTTP release receiver.
- Carried from the README: old-build retirement, contract attestation, operational hardening, and the memory ceiling are out of scope and unbuilt.

| Spike B scenario, `/tmp/exo-qual-b-combined-1` | B-1..B-6 pass | observed-real, fixture Director | `evidence/spike-b/final-combined.json` |
| Spike C synthetic, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-syn-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-synthetic | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-synthetic.json` |
| Spike C **live**, `/tmp/exo-qual-c-combined-live-1` | C-1..C-5 pass | observed-real, **live** `gpt-6-sol`, account `sha256:188b022d6e97` | `evidence/spike-c/final-combined-live.json` |

The combined live run in detail:
- 5 text turns, **11 model calls and 6 tool calls** in total. The heaviest turn used 3 model calls and 2 tool calls, against a limit of 4/4/90 s.
- The Task was observed `working` → `input-required`, followed by exactly one accepted abort and 0 releases.

**All three spikes pass their pre-registered checks, on each spike branch and again on the merged tree** (final combined run below). Each spike also exposed one real defect that the checks or the review caught before integration:
